363326.title: Bressoud's multi-summation conjecture for restricted partitions
363326.statement:
Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda$ and $\eta$ be integers satisfying

$$
0<\alpha_1<\alpha_2<\cdots<\alpha_\lambda<\eta,\qquad \alpha_i=\eta-\alpha_{\lambda+1-i}\quad(1\leq i\leq\lambda).
$$

For $k\geq r\geq\lambda\geq0$, let $B(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ whose parts are congruent to $0,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda$ modulo $\eta$, with only multiples of $\eta$ repeatable, satisfying the stated difference and small-parts conditions. Write $(a;q)_m$ for the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol and $(a;q)_\infty$ for its infinite counterpart. **Bressoud's conjecture.** For all such parameters,

$$
\sum_{n\geq0}B(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\lambda;\eta,k,r;n)q^n
=\sum_{N_1\geq\cdots\geq N_{k-1}\geq0}\frac{q^{\eta(N_1^2+\cdots+N_{k-1}^2+N_r+\cdots+N_{k-1})}}{(q^\eta;q^\eta)_{N_1-N_2}\cdots(q^\eta;q^\eta)_{N_{k-2}-N_{k-1}}(q^{\eta};q^{\eta})_{N_{k-1}}}
$$

$$
\qquad\times\prod_{s=1}^{\lambda}(-q^{\eta-\alpha_s-\eta N_s};q^\eta)_{N_s}\prod_{s=2}^{\lambda}(-q^{\eta-\alpha_s+\eta N_{s-1}};q^\eta)_\infty.
$$

This is a proposed generating-function identity for Bressoud's restricted partition function; the supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
363326.source_name: Y. H. Chen and Thomas Y. He, “A bijection related to Bressoud's conjecture”, arXiv:2405.19918 (2024).
363326.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19918

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363327.title: Flammenkamp's conjecture on exponential periods in subtraction games
363327.statement: Let a **subtraction game** be played on the non-negative integers using a finite ruleset $S\subset\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,\ldots\}$. The current player subtracts an element of $S$ when possible, and the player unable to move loses. The **eventual period length** is the period of the outcome sequence after a finite preperiod. **Flammenkamp's conjecture.** There exists a sequence of subtraction games on finite rulesets with an exponential eventual period length of the outcomes, with respect to the largest member of the subtraction set. This challenges the classical expectation that period lengths are bounded polynomially in the largest subtraction.
363327.source_name: Urban Larsson and Indrajit Saha, “A brief conversation about subtraction games”, arXiv:2405.20054 (2024).
363327.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20054

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363337.title: Divisor class group conjecture for Lovász–Saks–Schrijver rings of forests
363337.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a forest, let $\d=d=\Delta(G)+1$, and let $R_G(d)$ denote its Lovász–Saks–Schrijver ring. Write $\delta(v)$ for the degree of a vertex $v$ in $G$, and set

$$
m=\left|\{v\in V:\delta(v)=\Delta(G)\}\right|.
$$

**Divisor class group conjecture.** The divisor class group of $R_G(d)$ is

$$
\operatorname{Cl}(R_G(d))\cong\mathbb{Z}^m.
$$

This conjecture refines the paper's results on factoriality and divisor class groups for Lovász–Saks–Schrijver rings of forests, including explicit computations for star and path graphs. It predicts that the class group at the normality threshold $d=\Delta(G)+1$ is free abelian with one generator for each vertex of maximum degree; the source provides computational evidence but does not report a proof.
363337.source_name: Eliana Tolosa-Villarreal, “Normality, factoriality and strong F-regularity of Lovász-Saks-Schrijver rings”, arXiv:2405.20480 (2024).
363337.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20480

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363363.title: Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
363363.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Write $\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)$ for its covariance matrix, $\|\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)\|_{op}$ for its operator norm, and $C_P(\mu)$ for its Poincaré constant.

**Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\|\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)\|_{op} \leq C_P(\mu) \leq C\,\|\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)\|_{op}.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the Poincaré constant of every log-concave measure is controlled, up to universal factors, by the largest variance of a linear function. It is a central problem concerning bottlenecks and functional inequalities in high-dimensional convexity; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
363363.source_name: Bo'az Klartag and Joseph Lehec, “Isoperimetric inequalities in high-dimensional convex sets”, arXiv:2406.01324 (2024).
363363.references:
**7 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2306.12997](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12997), [arXiv:1810.08369](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.08369), [arXiv:1203.0893](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0893), [arXiv:1003.4839](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.4839), [arXiv:0801.4036](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.4036), [arXiv:0712.4092](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.4092).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01324

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363375.title: Conjecture on $j$-invariants of isogenous elliptic curves
363375.statement:
Let $K$ be a discrete valuation field of residue characteristic $2$, with valuation $v$ and ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Let $E_1/K$ and $E_2/K$ be elliptic curves, and suppose there is an isogeny of odd degree $d$ from $E_1/K$ to $E_2/K$. Assume that

$$
0<v(j(E_1))<15v(2).
$$

**$j$-invariant conjecture.** Then

$$
v(j(E_1))=v(j(E_2)).
$$

This conjecture aims to determine the reduction types of isogenous elliptic curves over discrete valuation fields of residue characteristic $2$ when $v(2)\geq 2$. It generalizes the preceding result for elliptic curves with additive reduction and good supersingular reduction after a quadratic extension, but its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
363375.source_name: Haiyang Wang, “On the Kodaira types of elliptic curves with potentially good supersingular reduction”, arXiv:2406.01985 (2024).
363375.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01985

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363379.title: The first- and second-degree bound for Snort temperature
363379.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. In the impartial graph game **Snort**, let $t(G)$ denote the temperature of the position on $G$, let $\deg(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$, and let $\deg_2(G)$ be the maximum number of vertices at distance $2$ from any vertex of $G$. **The first- and second-degree bound.** When playing Snort on $G$, one has

$$
t(G) \leq \deg(G) + \frac{1}{2}\deg_2(G).
$$

The paper has shown that Snort temperature cannot be bounded by a multiple of the degree, while this conjecture proposes that the first and second degrees suffice for a bound. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
363379.source_name: Svenja Huntemann and Tomasz Maciosowski, “Degrees are Useless in SNORT When Measuring Temperature”, arXiv:2406.02107 (2024).
363379.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02107

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363401.title: The short most frequent subword conjecture
363401.statement:
Let $w$ be a word of length at least $2$. A subword is **most frequent** if it maximizes the number of occurrences in $w$. **Short-subword conjecture.** At least one most frequent subword of $w$ has length at most

$$
\left\lceil \frac{|w|}{2} \right\rceil.
$$

The claim is motivated by lower bounds on maximum subword occurrence counts and by the intuition that sufficiently long subwords cannot be optimal. It is presented as open.
363401.source_name: Wenjie Fang, “Maximal number of subword occurrences in a word”, arXiv:2406.02971 (2025).
363401.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02971

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363407.title: Particle filter optimization parameter-selection conjectures
363407.statement:
Let $k_{max}$ be the maximum number of iterations, let $\lambda$ be the unscented-transform scaling factor, let $N$ be the number of particles, and let $Q$ be the state-transition covariance. The parameter analysis considers these quantities at high, low, or moderate levels, and compares the resulting optimization solutions.

**Parameter-selection conjecture.** It is likely to reach a better solution with lower $k_{max}$ and $\lambda$ when $N$ and $Q$ are high. The results suggest a correlation between $k_{max}$ and $N$, and between $\lambda$ and $Q$.

This claim is based on random-sampling experiments for parameter selection in single-variable optimization and is suggested to extend to relatively higher dimensions. Its status is not established beyond the reported experiments.
363407.source_name: Mostafa Eslami and Maryam Babazadeh, “Particle Filter Optimization: A Bayesian Approach for Global Stochastic Optimization”, arXiv:2406.03089 (2025).
363407.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03089

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363417.title: Conjecture on the largest noncyclic abelian group with a 2-element spanning set
363417.statement:
Let $s\geq 3$ be an integer. An $s$-spanning set of size $2$ in a finite abelian group is a set of two elements whose signed sums of at most $s$ terms cover the group. **Largest noncyclic group conjecture.** If $2s+1$ is prime, then the largest noncyclic group with an $s$-spanning set of size $2$ has order $2s^2$. If $2s+1$ is composite and $p$ is its smallest prime divisor, then the largest such noncyclic group has order

$$
2s^2+2s-\frac{p^2-1}{2}.
$$

In particular, every noncyclic group $G$ with an $s$-spanning set of size $2$ satisfies

$$
|G|\leq 2s^2+2s-4.
$$

The cyclic case is known, while the noncyclic case remains open when $s\not\equiv 1\pmod 3$.
363417.source_name: Bela Bajnok and W. Kyle Beatty, “On the Diameter of Undirected Cayley Graphs of Finite Abelian Groups”, arXiv:2406.04045 (2024).
363417.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04045

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

solutions.body:
Put
\[
B_s=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2:|x|+|y|\leq s\},
\qquad L=2s+1.
\]
Let \(G\) be a noncyclic finite abelian group with an \(s\)-spanning pair \(a,b\). The surjection
\[
\pi:\mathbb Z^2\longrightarrow G,\qquad (x,y)\longmapsto xa+yb,
\]
has kernel \(\Lambda\). Since \(G\) is noncyclic and two-generated,
\[
G\cong\mathbb Z_c\times\mathbb Z_{ck}
\]
for some \(c\geq2\). Choose a prime \(p\mid c\). Smith normal form implies
\[
\Lambda\subseteq p\mathbb Z^2.
\]
Therefore reduction modulo \(p\) induces a surjection
\[
G\twoheadrightarrow(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^2,
\]
each fiber having size \(|G|/p^2\). Since \(\pi(B_s)=G\), every residue class contains at least \(|G|/p^2\) points of \(B_s\). Hence
\[
|G|\leq p^2\mu_p(s),
\qquad
\mu_p(s)=
\min_{\rho\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^2}
|B_s\cap(\rho+p\mathbb Z^2)|. \tag{1}
\]

For odd \(p\), write
\[
L=pm+r,\qquad 0\leq r<p.
\]
The invertible change of coordinates modulo \(p\)
\[
u=x+y,\qquad v=x-y
\]
identifies \(B_s\) with pairs
\[
(u,v)\in[-s,s]^2,\qquad u\equiv v\pmod2.
\]
For a residue \(\alpha\pmod p\), let \(E_\alpha,O_\alpha\) count respectively the even and odd integers in \([-s,s]\) congruent to \(\alpha\). Set
\[
n_\alpha=E_\alpha+O_\alpha,\qquad
\delta_\alpha=E_\alpha-O_\alpha.
\]
Then the occupancy of the residue pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) equals
\[
E_\alpha E_\beta+O_\alpha O_\beta
=\frac{n_\alpha n_\beta+\delta_\alpha\delta_\beta}{2}. \tag{2}
\]

Exactly \(r\) residue classes have size \(m+1\), and \(p-r\) have size \(m\). Furthermore,
\[
\delta_\alpha=0\ \text{if }n_\alpha\text{ is even},
\qquad
\delta_\alpha\in\{-1,1\}\ \text{if }n_\alpha\text{ is odd}.
\]
Ordering residue classes by first appearance in the interval, the \(p-r\) minimum-size classes occur consecutively, and their \(\delta\)-signs alternate whenever \(m\) is odd. It follows from (2) that
\[
\mu_p(s)=
\begin{cases}
m^2/2,&m\text{ even},\\[2mm]
(m^2-1)/2,&m\text{ odd},\ r\leq p-2,\\[2mm]
(m^2+1)/2,&m\text{ odd},\ r=p-1.
\end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the middle case has two minimum-size classes with opposite signs. In the last case there is exactly one minimum-size class, and its self-pair gives \((m^2+1)/2\); every pair involving a size-\((m+1)\) class has occupancy at least \(m(m+1)/2\).

If \(p\mid L\), then \(r=0\) and \(m\) is odd, so
\[
|G|
\leq\frac{p^2(m^2-1)}2
=\frac{L^2-p^2}{2}
=
2s^2+2s-\frac{p^2-1}{2}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(p\nmid L\), then \(r\geq1\). The first two cases of (3) give
\[
p^2\mu_p(s)\leq\frac{(L-1)^2}{2}=2s^2.
\]
In the third case, \(r=p-1\), the same conclusion reduces to
\[
p^2(m^2+1)\leq(pm+p-2)^2.
\]
The difference between right and left is
\[
2pm(p-2)-4p+4,
\]
which is positive for \(p\geq5,m\geq1\), and for \(p=3\) whenever the odd integer \(m\geq3\). The sole exceptional case \(p=3,m=1\) gives \(s=2\), outside the hypothesis. Thus
\[
p\nmid L,\ s\geq3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|G|\leq2s^2. \tag{5}
\]

For \(p=2\), exactly \(s^2\) points of \(B_s\) satisfy
\[
x+y\not\equiv s\pmod2.
\]
If \(s\) is even, these split equally between the residue classes \((0,1)\) and \((1,0)\), giving
\[
\mu_2(s)\leq s^2/2.
\]
If \(s\) is odd, they occupy \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\), giving
\[
\mu_2(s)\leq(s^2-1)/2.
\]
Equation (1) again yields \(|G|\leq2s^2\).

If \(L=2s+1\) is prime, a prime \(p\mid c\) cannot equal \(L\): formula (3) would give \(\mu_L(s)=0\), contradicting spanning. Therefore \(p\nmid L\), and
\[
|G|\leq2s^2.
\]
If \(L\) is composite and \(p_0\) is its least prime divisor, either \(p\nmid L\), yielding (5), or \(p\mid L\), in which case \(p\geq p_0\) and (4) gives
\[
|G|
\leq
2s^2+2s-\frac{p_0^2-1}{2}.
\]
Since \(p_0^2\leq L\), this bound exceeds \(2s^2\) and therefore covers both cases.

Finally, both upper bounds are attained by the constructions already established in Theorem 1.7. The group
\[
\mathbb Z_s\times\mathbb Z_{2s}
\]
has the \(s\)-spanning pair
\[
\{(0,1),(1,1)\}
\]
and order \(2s^2\). If \(L=p_0t\), the group
\[
\mathbb Z_{p_0}
\times
\mathbb Z_{p_0(t^2-1)/2}
\]
has the \(s\)-spanning pair
\[
\left\{
\left(1,\frac{t-1}{2}\right),
\left(1,\frac{t+1}{2}\right)
\right\}
\]
and order
\[
\frac{L^2-p_0^2}{2}
=
2s^2+2s-\frac{p_0^2-1}{2}.
\]
These matching upper and lower bounds prove both cases of the conjecture for every \(s\geq3\).

363428.title: Multicolour induced size Ramsey conjecture for bounded-degree trees
363428.statement:
Let $cDelta\textgreater=1$, and let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $cDelta(T)\textgreater= cDelta$. For $q\textgreater=1$, write $crhat_{\mathrm{ind}}^q(T)$ for the $q$-colour induced size Ramsey number and $crhat^q(T)$ for the $q$-colour size Ramsey number. **Multicolour induced size Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
\hat r_{\mathrm{ind}}^q(T)=O_\Delta(\hat r^q(T)).
$$

The conjecture asks whether, for bounded-degree trees, induced and ordinary size Ramsey numbers have the same order as functions of the number of colours. The source gives no resolution.
363428.source_name: António Girão and Eoin Hurley, “Embedding induced trees in sparse expanding graphs”, arXiv:2406.04260 (2024).
363428.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04260

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024).

363432.title: Ramaswamy's conjecture on fail points
363432.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a planar convex domain symmetric about the two coordinate axes. A **fail point** is a point where $|\nabla u_{\Omega}|$ attains its maximum, where $u_{\Omega}$ is the torsion function. The largest inscribed circle is a circle of maximal radius contained in $\Omega$.

**Ramaswamy's conjecture.** The fail points occur either at the contact points of the largest inscribed circle or at points of minimal curvature.

This modified conjecture was proposed after Saint-Venant's conjecture was disproved and has been widely accepted in the mechanical engineering community. The source gives no resolution of Ramaswamy's conjecture.
363432.source_name: Qinfeng Li, Shuangquan Xie, Hang Yang and Ruofei Yao, “On the location of the maximal gradient of the torsion function over some non-symmetric planar domains”, arXiv:2406.04790 (2026).
363432.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04790

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2024). “Later, Ramaswamy and Sweers disproved Saint-Venant's conjecture by constructing domains symmetric about two axes such that the long and short axes are of equal length but the endpoints have different curvatures.”

363434.title: Strong Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture
363434.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $d$ and $k$ be positive integers. Define the **fractional arboricity** of $G$ by

$$
\gamma(G)=\max_{H\subseteq G,\,v(H)\geq 2}\frac{e(H)}{v(H)-1}.
$$

**Strong Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture.** If

$$
\gamma(G)\leq k+\frac{d}{d+k+1},
$$

then there is a partition of $G$ into $k+1$ forests such that, in one forest, every connected component has at most $d$ edges.

The conjecture strengthens the Nine Dragon Tree Theorem, which requires only that one forest have maximum degree $d$. It is known when $d\leq k+1$ and when $d\leq 2(k+1)$; all other cases remain open.
363434.source_name: Sebastian Mies and Benjamin Moore, “An Approximate Version of the Strong Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture”, arXiv:2406.05022 (2024).
363434.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2310.00931](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00931), [arXiv:2208.06336](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06336), [arXiv:2201.10791](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10791), [arXiv:1905.02600](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.02600), [arXiv:1904.12435](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12435).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05022

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363489.title: Even-torus conjecture for optimal plaid solutions
363489.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ be even, and let $(B,W)$ be an $(a,b)$-plaid on the torus $\mathbb{T}_n$ for which $\min\{|B|,|W|\}$ is maximum. **Even-torus conjecture.** Then

$$
t(n)\leqslant 2+\min\{|B|,|W|\}.
$$

The conjecture formalizes the observation that swapped optimal plaid solutions have at most two more black queens than an optimal $(a,b)$-plaid. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
363489.source_name: Katie Clinch, Matthew Drescher, Tony Huynh and Abdallah Saffidine, “Constructions, bounds, and algorithms for peaceable queens”, arXiv:2406.06974 (2024).
363489.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06974

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363522.title: Galois equivariance of the semisimple local Langlands correspondence
363522.statement:
Suppose the semisimple local Langlands correspondence $bbLL_{bbG}$ exists. Let $bbsigma$ be an automorphism of $bbC$ fixing $bqsqrt q$, and let $(bbM,bbrho)$ be a supercuspidal-support datum for $bbG$. **Galois-equivariance conjecture.** One has

$$
bbLL_{bbG}(bbrho^{bbsigma})=bbLL_{bbG}(bbrho)^{bbsigma}.
$$

The source introduces this conjecture to descend results to the smallest possible base ring. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
363522.source_name: Jean-François Dat, David Helm, Robert Kurinczuk and Gilbert Moss, “Local Langlands in families: The banal case”, arXiv:2406.09283 (2024).
363522.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09283

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363548.title: Steinhaus's conjecture on the isoperimetric ratio of Euclidean tilings
363548.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tiling of the Euclidean plane whose tiles all have diameter at least $D$, for some fixed $D>0$. For each cell $C$ of $\mathcal{T}$, its isoperimetric ratio is

$$
\frac{\operatorname{perim}(C)^2}{\operatorname{area}(C)}.
$$

**Steinhaus's conjecture.** The maximum isoperimetric ratio among the cells of $\mathcal{T}$ is minimal when $\mathcal{T}$ is a regular hexagonal tiling. The source recalls this as Problem C15 in the cited reference and provides no resolution, so its status remains open.
363548.source_name: Zsolt Lángi and Shanshan Wang, “The Honeycomb Conjecture in normed planes and an alpha-convex variant of a theorem of Dowker”, arXiv:2406.10622 (2025).
363548.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10622

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024). “This conjecture was proved by L. Fejes T\'oth for convex tilings, and by Hales for not necessarily convex tilings.”

363584.title: Penalty relaxation feasibility bound for convex constrained optimization
363584.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ define a convex constrained optimization problem of the form

$$
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g(x)\leq 0.
$$

For a penalty parameter $\Lambda$, consider the penalty relaxation

$$
\min_x f(x)+\Lambda [g(x)]_+,
$$

where $[g(x)]_+$ denotes the positive part of $g(x)$, and let $\Delta(\delta)$ denote the quantity appearing in the source's Slater-type bound. **Penalty relaxation feasibility conjecture.** The penalty relaxation can guarantee $\delta$-feasibility whenever $\delta$ solves

$$
\delta\geq\frac{\Delta(\delta)}{\Lambda}.
$$

This is presented as following from a Slater-type argument, but the source does not provide enough surrounding definitions to determine the precise meaning of $\Delta(\delta)$ or whether the claim has been established as a theorem.
363584.source_name: Guy Kornowski, Swati Padmanabhan, Kai Wang, Zhe Zhang and Suvrit Sra, “First-Order Methods for Linearly Constrained Bilevel Optimization”, arXiv:2406.12771 (2025).
363584.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12771

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363606.title: Infinite strict log-concavity conjecture for transposed Boros-Moll sequences
363606.statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ be the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$, and consider, for fixed $\ell$, the transposed sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the operator on sequences defined by $\mathcal{L}(\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0})=\{a_i^2-a_{i-1}a_{i+1}\}_{i\geq 0}$, with $a_{-1}=0$. A sequence is **$\infty$-strictly-log-concave** if every iterate $\mathcal{L}^j$ is strictly positive. **Transposed Boros-Moll conjecture.** The transposed Boros-Moll sequences $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ are $\infty$-strictly-log-concave for any $\ell\geq 3$. Numerical experiments support the conjecture, while the cases $\ell=0,1,2$ exhibit obstructions described in the source.
363606.source_name: James J. Y. Zhao, “The extended reverse ultra log-concavity of transposed Boros-Moll sequences”, arXiv:2406.13790 (2024).
363606.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13790

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024). “Boros and Moll showed that the sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{\ell=0}^m$ is unimodal with the maximum term located in the middle, see also . Moll further conjectured that the sequences $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{\ell=0}^m$ are log-concave, which”

363613.title: Aharoni's transversal Dirac conjecture
363613.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G} = \{G_1, \ldots, G_n\}$ be a collection of graphs with common vertex set $V$ of size $n$. Define $\delta(\mathcal{G})=\min\{\delta(G_i):1\leq i\leq n\}$, where $\delta(G_i)$ is the minimum degree of $G_i$. A **transversal Hamilton cycle** is a Hamilton cycle whose edges can be assigned distinct representatives from the graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_n$, with the edge assigned to $G_i$ belonging to $G_i$. **Aharoni's transversal Dirac conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(\mathcal{G})\geq \frac{n}{2},
$$

then $\mathcal{G}$ contains a transversal Hamilton cycle. This conjecture extends Dirac's Hamilton-cycle theorem to graph collections; it was solved asymptotically by Cheng, Wang and Zhao and completely confirmed by Joos and Kim.
363613.source_name: Yangyang Cheng, Wanting Sun, Guanghui Wang and Lan Wei, “Transversal Hamilton paths and cycles”, arXiv:2406.13998 (2024).
363613.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13998

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024). “Cheng, Wang and Zhao solved this conjecture asymptotically, and it was completely confirmed by Joos and Kim .”

363683.title: Adamus–Adamus conjecture on long cycles in balanced bipartite graphs
363683.statement:
Let $G$ be a balanced bipartite graph of order $2n$, with minimum degree $delta(G)\ge r\ge 1$, where $n\ge 2k+2r$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. **Adamus–Adamus conjecture.** If

$$
e(G)>n(n-k-r)+r(k+r),
$$

then $G$ contains a cycle of length $2n-2k$. This is presented as the criterion proposed by Adamus and Adamus for guaranteeing a prescribed long cycle; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or remains open.
363683.source_name: Changchang Dong, Mei Lu, Jixiang Meng and Bo Ning, “The generalized Tur'an number of long cycles in graphs and bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2406.17371 (2024).
363683.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17371

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363691.title: The cycles plus $K_4$'s conjecture
363691.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $2$, and let $G$ be obtained from $H$ by gluing on vertex-disjoint copies of $K_4$. **Cycles plus $K_4$'s conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi(G)\leq 4.
$$

The conjecture allows paths in the base graph as well as cycles, although it suffices to prove it for $2$-regular $H$, since the other cases are subgraphs of those instances. The source describes this as a seemingly very difficult conjecture and proves only that the path-linked triangles 3-colourability conjecture implies it.
363691.source_name: Aseem Dalal, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “A reduction of the "cycles plus K_4's" problem”, arXiv:2406.17723 (2024).
363691.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17723

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “On the other hand, while the truth of the Strong Colouring Conjecture is trivial for $\Delta(H)=1$, (where it asks essentially for the union of two matchings to be bipartite), the $\Delta(H)=c$ case is open for all constants $c\geq 2$.”

363698.title: The even-dimensional extremal-size conjecture for intersecting temperate families
363698.statement:
Let $n=2k$ be even, and let an **intersecting temperate family** on $[n]$ be a temperate family in which every two members have non-empty intersection. **Even intersecting-temperate-family conjecture.** The maximum size of an intersecting temperate family on $[n]$ is

$$
\frac{1}{2}\binom{2k}{k}+\binom{2k}{k+1}+\binom{2k-1}{k+2}.
$$

This is the even-$n$ counterpart of the proved extremal result for odd $n$; the exact maximum in the even case remains open.
363698.source_name: Jan Petr and Pavel Turek, “Towards odd-sunflowers: temperate families and lightnings”, arXiv:2406.18437 (2024).
363698.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18437

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “This conjecture, known as the Sunflower Conjecture, is unresolved to this date.”

363749.title: Syzygy behavior in the base locus decomposition program
363749.statement:
Let $U$ be a sheaf on the relevant moduli space, and let $W$ be a wall of its stable base locus decomposition. A sheaf is called **$F$-admissible** when its syzygies arise from the Bridgeland destabilizing object $F$ associated with that wall.

**Syzygy behavior conjecture.** A sheaf $U$ is $F$-admissible, where $F$ is a Bridgeland destabilizing object that yields the wall $W$ when $U$ enters the stable base locus at the wall $W$.

This statement is presented as the syzygy behavior suggested by the authors' analysis of how minimal free resolutions and interpolation problems determine walls in stable base locus decompositions. The supplied text does not establish its general validity or provide evidence resolving it.
363749.source_name: Manuel Leal, Cesar Lozano Huerta and Tim Ryan, “Geometry of syzygies of sheaves on P^2 via interpolation and Bridgeland stability”, arXiv:2407.00526 (2024).
363749.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00526

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363759.title: The chromatic-polynomial characterization of signed complete graphs
363759.statement:
Let $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ be signed complete graphs. Write $\Sigma_1\cong\Sigma_2$ when they are isomorphic, and let $\mathscr B(\Sigma,x,y)$ and $\mathsf E(\Sigma,x,y)$ denote their bivariate and ordinary chromatic polynomials, respectively. **Signed complete-graph characterization conjecture.**

$$
\Sigma_1 \cong \Sigma_2 \iff \mathscr B(\Sigma_1,x,y) = \mathscr B(\Sigma_2,x,y) \iff \mathsf E(\Sigma_1,x,y) = \mathsf E(\Sigma_2,x,y).
$$

Thus, within signed complete graphs, both polynomials are conjectured to determine the graph up to isomorphism. The source gives this as a conjecture and does not provide a resolution.
363759.source_name: Gary R. W. Greaves, Jeven Syatriadi and Charissa I. Utomo, “Chromatic polynomials of signed graphs and dominating-vertex deletion formulae”, arXiv:2407.00883 (2024).
363759.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00883

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363785.title: Füredi–Jiang–Kostochka–Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture for ordered hypergraph forests
363785.statement:
Let $F$ be an $r$-uniform forest with interval chromatic number $r$. **Füredi–Jiang–Kostochka–Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture.** The maximum number of edges in a vertex-ordered $r$-uniform hypergraph with no subgraph order-isomorphic to $F$ is

$$
O\bigl(n^{r-1}\log^{c(F)}n\bigr)
$$

for some constant $c(F)$. This extends the Pach–Tardos conjecture from ordered graphs to ordered uniform hypergraphs; the case $r=2$ is stated to be equivalent to it.
363785.source_name: Seth Pettie and Gábor Tardos, “A Refutation of the Pach-Tardos Conjecture for 0-1 Matrices”, arXiv:2407.02638 (2024).
363785.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02638

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2024).

363816.title: The supersaturation conjecture for independent transversals
363816.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a $(2\Delta)$-thick partition of $V(G)$. An **independent transversal** is a set containing exactly one vertex from each part of $\mathcal{U}$ and inducing no edges in $G$. **Supersaturation conjecture.** The number of independent transversals of $(G,\mathcal{U})$ is minimised when $G$ is a disjoint union of $|\mathcal{U}|$ copies of $K_{\Delta,\Delta}$. This conjecture proposes a sharp supersaturation-type strengthening of Haxell's theorem; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
363816.source_name: Pjotr Buys, Ross J. Kang and Kenta Ozeki, “Reconfiguration of Independent Transversals”, arXiv:2407.04367 (2024).
363816.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04367

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363827.title: Weak Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture with a moving target
363827.statement:
Let $\rho:
\mathbb N\to[0,\a0\infty)$ be an arbitrary function satisfying

$$
\sum_{q\in\mathbb N}\left(\frac{\varphi(q)\rho(q)}{q}\right)^2=\infty,
$$

and let $\mathbf y=(\mathbf y_q)_{q\in\mathbb N}$ be an arbitrary sequence in $\mathbb R^2$. Write $W_2'(\mathbf y,\rho)$ for the set of $\mathbf x\in[0,1]^2$ satisfying the corresponding infinitely-often inhomogeneous approximation inequalities with coordinatewise coprimality, and let $\lambda_2$ denote Lebesgue measure.

**Weak Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture with a moving target.** For every such $\rho$ and $\mathbf y$,

$$
\lambda_2\left(W_2'(\mathbf y,\rho)\right)=1.
$$

This is the conjectured two-dimensional moving-target analogue of the inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer theorem. The paper presents it as open; a preceding counterexample for a moving target does not disprove this weak formulation.
363827.source_name: Manuel Hauke and Felipe A. Ramirez, “The Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture with a moving target”, arXiv:2407.05344 (2024).
363827.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.05344

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2024). “The Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture was proved in a breakthrough result by Koukoulopoulos and Maynard in 2020.”

363831.title: Harutyunyan–Mohar conjecture for oriented graphs
363831.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, meaning a digraph with no biclique of order greater than $1$. Let $\widetilde{\Delta}(D)=\max_{v\in V(D)}\sqrt{d^+(v)d^-(v)}$ be its maximum geometric mean of in- and out-degrees, and let $\vec\chi(D)$ be its dichromatic number, the minimum number of colours whose colour classes induce acyclic subdigraphs.

**Harutyunyan–Mohar conjecture.** Every oriented graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\vec\chi(D)\leq\left\lceil\frac{\widetilde{\Delta}(D)}{2}\right\rceil+1.
$$

This is the proposed oriented-graph analogue of Reed's conjecture. The paper records partial upper bounds but leaves this conjecture open.
363831.source_name: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi and Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta, “An analogue of Reed's conjecture for digraphs”, arXiv:2407.05827 (2025).
363831.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1409.7535](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.7535).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.05827

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363857.title: Kirillov–Bazhanov–Reshetikhin dilogarithm identity for constant Y-systems
363857.statement:
Let $X$ be a simply-laced connected Dynkin diagram of finite type with rank $r$, Coxeter number $h=h(X)$, and vertex set $I=1,\dots,r1$. Let $\ell\geq 2$ and let $y_m^{(a)}1\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ for $a\in I$ and $m=1,\dots,\ell-1$ be a positive real solution of the constant $Y$-system described in the source, with boundary values $y_0^{(a)}{}^{-1}=y_\ell^{(a)}{}^{-1}=0$. Here $h=r+1$ for $A_r$, $h=2r-2$ for $D_r$, and $h=12,18,30$ for $E_6,E_7,E_8$, respectively. **Kirillov–Bazhanov–Reshetikhin conjecture.** For these values, one has

$$
\sum_{a=1}^r\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}\tilde{L}(y_m^{(a)})=\frac{r(\ell-1)h}{h+\ell}\frac{\pi^2}{6}.
$$

The identity arose from the thermodynamic analysis of restricted solid-on-solid models and predicts a uniform dilogarithm evaluation for all simply-laced finite Dynkin types and levels. The source presents it as a conjecture of Kirillov, Bazhanov, and Reshetikhin; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
363857.source_name: Tomoki Nakanishi, “Cluster Algebras and Dilogarithm Identities”, arXiv:2407.06668 (2025).
363857.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363861.title: The minimum size conjecture for quasirandom-forcing sets of 4-point permutations
363861.statement:
A set of permutations is **quasirandom-forcing** if forcing the corresponding permutation densities determines the uniform measure on $[0,1]^2$. The paper has shown that every such set of $4$-point permutations has at least five elements, and examples with eight elements are known.

**Minimum size conjecture for 4-point permutations.** Every quasirandom-forcing set of $4$-point permutations has cardinality at least eight.

The conjecture asserts that the known upper bound of eight is tight, so the minimum cardinality is exactly eight.
363861.source_name: Daniel Kráľ, Jae-baek Lee and Jonathan A. Noel, “Forcing quasirandomness with 4-point permutations”, arXiv:2407.06869 (2024).
363861.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06869

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363921.title: Aharoni–Berger conjecture on coloring intersections of two matroids
363921.statement:
Let $V$ be a common ground set, and let $d4d8_1$ and $d4d8_2$ be matroids on $V$. For a matroid or complex $d4d8$, let $d712(d4d8)$ denote the minimum number of independent sets, or faces, whose union is its ground set.

**Aharoni–Berger conjecture.** For any two matroids $d4d8_1$ and $d4d8_2$ on the same ground set,

$$
\chi(\mathcal{M}_1\cap\mathcal{M}_2)\le\max\bigl(\chi(\mathcal{M}_1),\chi(\mathcal{M}_2)+1\bigr).
$$

Aharoni and Berger proved the weaker bound $\chi(\mathcal{M}_1\cap\mathcal{M}_2)\le 2\max(\chi(\mathcal{M}_1),\chi(\mathcal{M}_2))$, while a refined topological method gives the bound $\chi(\mathcal{M}_1\cap\mathcal{M}_2)\le\chi(\mathcal{M}_1)+\chi(\mathcal{M}_2)$. The stated bound remains open in the supplied source.
363921.source_name: He Guo, “The list chromatic number of the intersection of two generalized partition matroids”, arXiv:2407.08796 (2024).
363921.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08796

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363954.title: Drier–Linial conjecture on the Hajós number of random lifts
363954.statement: An $\ell$-lift of $K_n$ is obtained by replacing every vertex of $K_n$ with an independent set of size $\ell$ and every edge with a matching of size $\ell$ between the corresponding fibers. Say that almost all $\ell$-lifts of $K_n$ have a property if all but a vanishing proportion do as $n\to\infty$. The **Hajós number** of a graph is the largest order of a topological clique occurring as a subgraph. **Drier–Linial conjecture.** For $\ell\geq\Omega(n)$, almost all $\ell$-lifts of $K_n$ have Hajós number equal to $\Theta(n)$. Drier and Linial established a linear lower bound when $\ell<(1-o(1))n/2$, while the conjecture addresses the larger-lift regime; the supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.
363954.source_name: Matija Bucić, Micha Christoph, Alp Müyesser and Raphael Steiner, “Topological Minors in Typical Lifts”, arXiv:2407.10565 (2024).
363954.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10565

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2024). “This conjecture has been disproved by Catlin in 1979.”

363966.title: Houdré–Tetali conjecture on isoperimetric constants of reversible Markov chains
363966.statement:
Let $(V,P,pi)$ be an irreducible and reversible Markov chain. For $p\in[0,1]$, let $\varphi_p(P)$ denote its isoperimetric constant, and let $\lambda_2(I-P)$ be the second-smallest eigenvalue of $I-P$. **Houdré–Tetali conjecture.** One has

$$
\lambda_2(I-P) \lesssim \varphi_{\frac12}(P) \lesssim \sqrt{\lambda_2(I-P)}.
$$

This conjecture extends the hard direction of Cheeger's inequality from $\varphi_1$ to $\varphi_{\frac12}$ and would show that the intermediate isoperimetric constant is controlled by the spectral gap up to the same square-root bounds. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
363966.source_name: Lap Chi Lau and Dante Tjowasi, “On the Houdré-Tetali conjecture about an isoperimetric constant of graphs”, arXiv:2407.11357 (2024).
363966.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.11357

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364019.title: The Ratios Conjectures lemma for pair correlations of zeros
364019.statement:
Let $f_d$ be a quadratic twist in the family and define

$$
\mathcal{T}_{f_d}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=\int_0^T\frac{L(s+\alpha,f_d)L(1-s+\beta,\overline{f}_d)}{L(s+\gamma,f_d)L(1-s+\delta,\overline{f}_d)}\,dt,
$$

where $s=1/2+it$. For $-1/4<\operatorname{Re}(\alpha),\operatorname{Re}(\beta)<1/4$, $1/\log(T)\ll\operatorname{Re}(\delta)<1/4$, and $\operatorname{Im}(\alpha),\operatorname{Im}(\beta)\ll_{\varepsilon}T^{1-\varepsilon}$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, define $Y_U$ and $A_L$ by the Euler products in the source. **The Ratios Conjectures lemma.**

$$
\mathcal{T}_{f_d}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=\int_0^T\left(Y_U(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)A_L(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)+\left(\frac{\sqrt{M}|d|t}{2\pi}\right)^{-2(\alpha+\beta)}Y_U(-\beta,-\alpha,\gamma,\delta)A_L(-\beta,-\alpha,\gamma,\delta)\right)dt+O(T^{1/2+\varepsilon}).
$$

The formula is used, under GRH, to evaluate pair-correlation statistics for zeros without a Fourier-transform support restriction. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
364019.source_name: Owen Barrett, Zoë X. Batterman, Aditya Jambhale, Steven J. Miller, Akash L. Narayanan, Kishan Sharma and Chris Yao, “A Random Matrix Model for a Family of Cusp Forms”, arXiv:2407.14526 (2024).
364019.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14526

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364026.title: The logarithmic maximum-entry conjecture for tame random matrices
364026.statement:
Let $(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{c})$ be an $m\times n$ $\delta$-tame margin for a base measure $\mu$, and let $X\sim\lambda_{\mathbf{r},\mathbf{c}}$ be the corresponding margin-conditioned random matrix.

**Logarithmic maximum-entry conjecture.** With high probability,

$$
\max_{ij}X_{ij}\leq C\log(m+n)
$$

for some constant $C=C(\mu,\delta)>0$.

This conjecture extends the known logarithmic maximum-entry behavior from constant linear margins and classical Lebesgue or counting measures to general base measures and tame margins. The source notes that it remains unresolved in this broader setting.
364026.source_name: Hanbaek Lyu and Sumit Mukherjee, “Large random matrices with given margins”, arXiv:2407.14942 (2025).
364026.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14942

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2024). “This conjecture was established by Ngyuen .”

364027.title: Universality of the empirical spectral distribution without sub-Gaussianity
364027.statement:
Let $X$ be a random matrix with independent entries conditioned to have general $\delta$-tame margins, and let Theorem (ii) denote the empirical spectral distribution conclusion in the paper.

**Non-sub-Gaussian ESD conjecture.** The conclusion of Theorem (ii) holds without assuming that the base measure $\mu$ is sub-Gaussian.

The conjecture would extend the empirical spectral distribution theorem beyond sub-Gaussian entry laws. The source proposes deriving it using the logarithmic maximum-entry conjecture and truncation; it does not provide a resolution of this general statement.
364027.source_name: Hanbaek Lyu and Sumit Mukherjee, “Large random matrices with given margins”, arXiv:2407.14942 (2025).
364027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14942

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2024). “This conjecture was established by Ngyuen .”

364087.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the maximum spread of realizable bases
364087.statement:
Fix an even integer $k$. For a realizable basis

$$
I=\{a_1,a_1+1,a_2,a_2+1,\ldots,a_{k/2},a_{k/2}+1,n\},
$$

define its spread by $\operatorname{Sp}(I)=|a_{k/2}+1-a_1|$, and define

$$
\operatorname{Msp}(n,k)=\max\{\operatorname{Sp}(I_i):1\leq i\leq N\}.
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** For each fixed $k$, $\operatorname{Msp}(n,k)$ is a monotonic non-decreasing function of $n$. The conjecture is motivated by numerical tables of maximum spreads for collected values of $n$ and $k$; no proof or resolution is stated.
364087.source_name: Daniel Berend, Philip A. Ernst, Aryeh Kontorovich and Rishi Kumar, “Exact expressions for the maximal probability that all k-wise independent bits are 1”, arXiv:2407.18688 (2024).
364087.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18688

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364095.title: The set-palette conjecture for complete graphs
364095.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In a general edge-coloring of $K_n$, let $\tau_s(n)$ denote the minimum number of colors needed so that all triangles have distinct color palettes when a palette is viewed as the set of colors appearing on its three edges. **Set-palette conjecture.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\tau_s(n)=n-1.
$$

The source notes the inequality $\tau_m(n)\leq\tau_s(n)\leq\tau'(n)$ and states that this conjecture would imply the preceding multiset-palette conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
364095.source_name: Monika Pilsniak and Mariusz Wozniak, “A note on edge colorings distinguishing all triangles in a graph”, arXiv:2407.19050 (2024).
364095.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19050

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364097.title: Maximal-order uniqueness conjecture for maximal doubly even codes
364097.statement:
Let $C\subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a maximal doubly even binary code, and let $I=(i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{n-1})$. Consider the Clifford algebra $\mathbb{C}_n$ and the rational Clifford algebra $\left(\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{\mathbb{Q}}\right)$. **Maximal-order uniqueness conjecture.** For every maximal doubly even binary code $C\subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$, there exists a unique maximal order $\mathcal{O}_C\subset \left(\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{\mathbb{Q}}\right)\subset \mathbb{C}_n$ containing the Clifford order such that

$$
\mathcal{O}_C \supset \mathbb{Z}\left[\frac{c\cdot I}{2}:c\in C\right].
$$

The assertion is false: the Hurwitz order provides a counterexample to the related claim that every order equals the algebra generated by its vector part, so the proposed uniqueness statement does not hold in the stated generality.
364097.source_name: Taylor Dupuy, Anton Hilado, Colin Ingalls and Adam Logan, “The Basic Theory of Clifford-Bianchi Groups for Hyperbolic n-Space”, arXiv:2407.19122 (2024).
364097.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19122

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

364099.title: Single-bubble conjecture for Clifford-Euclidean orders
364099.statement:
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an order in the relevant Clifford algebra, and suppose that it is **Clifford-Euclidean**, meaning that it admits the Clifford-Euclidean division property used to construct its fundamental domain. A boundary bubble is one of the boundary spheres or bubbles occurring in that fundamental-domain construction. **Single-bubble conjecture.** If $\mathcal{O}$ is Clifford-Euclidean, then every boundary bubble has radius $1$, and there exists a fundamental domain requiring only a single bubble.
The claim is based on experimental observations; the source gives no proof or resolution.
364099.source_name: Taylor Dupuy, Anton Hilado, Colin Ingalls and Adam Logan, “The Basic Theory of Clifford-Bianchi Groups for Hyperbolic n-Space”, arXiv:2407.19122 (2024).
364099.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19122

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364118.title: The Cayley-equivalence maximum conjecture
364118.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be Cayley permutations of the same length, and let $\max(p)$ denote the largest letter occurring in $p$. Write $p\sim_c q$ for Cayley-equivalence. **The Cayley-equivalence maximum conjecture.** If

$$
p\sim_c q,
$$

then

$$
\max(p)=\max(q).
$$

The conjecture asks whether Cayley-equivalence forces the two patterns to have the same maximum letter. The source observes that the analogous conclusion is immediate for content-multiplicity equivalence, but leaves the Cayley-equivalence case as an open problem.
364118.source_name: Anders Claesson, Giulio Cerbai, Dana C. Ernst and Hannah Golab, “Pattern-avoiding Cayley permutations via combinatorial species”, arXiv:2407.19583 (2024).
364118.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).
